changelog: Replace C4 to remove a blanket ban on noun+modifier cuts and add a decision rule that allows such cuts when they prevent very-short, harmful splits (addresses primary_finding).
Paraphrase C5 shorter to save space while keeping the warning about fronted adjuncts' attachment needs.
Insert a new principle after C4 that flags cuts leaving only postverbal/postnominal adjuncts as high contradiction risk and prefers keeping modifiers attached.
Add a short worked example showing when to allow a noun+modifier split to preserve a subject/predicate (teaches the tradeoff concretely).

Replace C5 to explicitly flag postverbal/postnominal trailing adjuncts as high-contradiction risk and instruct scorers to keep such modifiers attached unless they form an independent proposition (addresses the primary finding about trailing fragments causing high contra).

Insert a short worked example after E4 that demonstrates allowing a noun+modifier cut to preserve a subject/predicate and avoid very-short harmful splits (addresses the primary_finding and obeys the examples_only constraint).

Insert a concise decision rule after C4 that allows noun+modifier cuts when forbidding them would force very-short (≈≤3–5 word) harmful splits, so scorers prefer preserving subjects/predicates; addresses the primary finding about an over-generalized ban on noun+modifier cuts.
